 Social Security’s 3.6% COLA Is Official — Here’s When You’ll See Your Exact 2027 Benefit Amount
 November 1, 2026 by Drew Blankenship 
 Social Security’s 3.6% COLA will increase the average retiree’s monthly benefit by approximately $75 in 2027. Personalized benefit notices will become available online in late November and arrive by mail in December. Helena Lopes/Pexels Millions of retirees finally have an answer to one of the biggest Social Security questions of the year. The Social Security Administration (SSA) officially announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 on October 14, 2026, giving beneficiaries a larger increase than they received this year. But knowing the percentage doesn’t necessarily tell you how much money will land in your bank account.
 According to the Social Security Administration , the increase will affect approximately 76 million Americans receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income (SSI). The average retired worker is expected to receive about $75 more per month, bringing the estimated average benefit to $2,170. However, Medicare premiums, benefit deductions, and individual payment amounts can change what retirees actually receive.
 Fortunately, Social Security has confirmed when beneficiaries can see their personalized 2027 Social Security COLA notices, including their exact new benefit amounts. Here’s what retirees should know before January arrives.
 The 3.6% Increase Is Now Official
 The SSA announced that Social Security retirement, survivor, disability, and SSI benefits will increase by 3.6% for 2027. That’s higher than the 2.8% adjustment beneficiaries received in 2026, providing some additional breathing room for households dealing with rising living expenses. The increase is calculated using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, commonly called the CPI-W. Specifically, the agency compares average inflation readings from the third quarter of one year with the corresponding period from the previous year. The 2027 Social Security COLA is automatic, meaning eligible beneficiaries don’t need to submit an application to receive the adjustment.
 Your Exact Benefit Amount May Be Available in Late November
 Beneficiaries won’t necessarily have to wait until January to learn their new monthly payment. According to the SSA’s October 14 announcement , personalized COLA notices will become available online starting in late November 2026. These notices will appear in the Message Center of eligible beneficiaries’ personal my Social Security accounts. The agency says people who want online access to their notices should establish an account and enroll in paperless notices by November 18, 2026. That deadline is particularly important for retirees who prefer reviewing their updated benefits before the traditional December mailing.
 Paper Notices Will Arrive in December
 If you don’t have an online Social Security account, there’s no need to worry about missing your benefit information. The SSA plans to mail personalized 2027 Social Security COLA notices to beneficiaries who haven’t enrolled in paperless delivery during December. These notices will explain the new monthly benefit amount and any applicable deductions in a simplified, one-page format. Some recipients may receive their letters earlier than others because mailing dates and delivery times can vary. Social Security advises beneficiaries to wait until January before contacting the agency about a mailed notice that hasn’t arrived.
 How Much More Money Could You Receive?
 The SSA’s official 2027 COLA fact sheet estimates that the average retired worker’s monthly benefit will increase from $2,095 to $2,170. That’s approximately $75 more each month, or $900 over a full year before considering any changes in deductions. Someone currently receiving a $1,500 monthly benefit could see a gross increase of approximately $54, bringing the payment to around $1,554. A retiree receiving $2,500 might see an increase of roughly $90, bringing the gross monthly benefit to approximately $2,590. These examples illustrate the 2027 Social Security COLA, but individual benefit calculations and deductions determine the actual amount deposited.
 Medicare Premiums Could Reduce Your Take-Home Increase
 One reason retirees should review their personalized notices is that a higher gross Social Security benefit doesn’t always translate into an equally large increase in take-home income. Many beneficiaries have Medicare Part B premiums deducted directly from their monthly Social Security payments. If those premiums increase in 2027, they could absorb part of the additional money provided by the COLA. Higher-income retirees may also pay income-related monthly adjustment amounts, known as IRMAA, which can further affect their deductions. Medicare-related information will be included in personalized notices, making it important to compare gross benefits with the final payment amount.
 SSI Recipients Will See Their Increase Earlier
 People receiving Supplemental Security Income follow a slightly different payment schedule than traditional Social Security retirement beneficiaries. Increased SSI payments for approximately 7.3 million recipients will begin on December 31, 2026. That’s because January 1 is a federal holiday, so the January SSI payment is issued on the preceding business day. The maximum federal SSI payment for an eligible individual will rise from $994 in 2026 to $1,029 in 2027, although actual payments depend on income, living arrangements, and other eligibility factors. People who receive both SSI and Social Security should review their notices carefully because the programs have different payment schedules and calculation rules.
 The January Payment Schedule Matters
 For most Social Security retirement beneficiaries, the 2027 Social Security COLA will first appear in their January 2027 payment. The agency generally distributes retirement benefits on the second, third, or fourth Wednesday of the month, depending on the beneficiary’s birth date. People who began receiving benefits before May 1997, along with certain other recipients, generally follow a different payment schedule. Beneficiaries should check the official Social Security payment calendar rather than assuming their money will arrive on January 1. Knowing the correct deposit date can help retirees schedule mortgage payments, utility bills, and other recurring expenses without risking an overdraft.
 Don’t Fall for COLA-Related Scams
 Whenever Social Security announces a benefit increase, scammers may attempt to exploit confusion surrounding the new payments. Fraudulent callers or emails may claim that beneficiaries must verify personal information, pay a processing fee, or provide banking details to activate their COLA. However, the 2027 Social Security COLA is applied automatically to eligible benefits without any special enrollment or payment requirement. The SSA’s Office of the Inspector General warns consumers to be suspicious of unexpected requests for Social Security numbers, account information, or payments. If you receive a questionable message, avoid clicking unfamiliar links and visit SSA.gov directly to access your account.
 What Retirees Should Do Before the End of 2026
 Now is a good time to confirm that Social Security has your correct mailing address and contact information. Beneficiaries who want early digital access should review their my Social Security account and enroll in paperless notices before the November 18 deadline. Once the personalized notice arrives, compare your current gross benefit, updated gross benefit, Medicare deductions, and expected net payment. If you rely heavily on Social Security for retirement income, consider updating your January household budget before scheduling major purchases or financial commitments. Even a modest monthly adjustment can make a meaningful difference when it’s planned for rather than absorbed by unexpected expenses.
 Your Personalized Notice Is the Number That Really Matters
 The official 2027 Social Security COLA of 3.6% is welcome news for millions of Americans trying to keep pace with inflation. However, the national average increase of $75 doesn’t necessarily reflect what every retiree will receive. Your personalized COLA notice will provide the most useful information, including your updated benefit amount and applicable deductions. Watch for online notices beginning in late November or mailed notices during December, and remember that the higher retirement payments generally begin in January. Reviewing those numbers before the new year can help you make smarter financial decisions and avoid surprises when your first 2027 deposit arrives.
 Are you satisfied with Social Security’s 3.6% increase for 2027, or do you think rising Medicare premiums, groceries, and housing costs will absorb most of it? Share your thoughts in the comments!
